text.p: Raith Rovers, who are all but relegated from the Scottish premier division, sacked manager Iain Munro on Monday after just seven months in the job.

Munro took over last September but Raith have spent the season languishing at the bottom of the table and their 5-0 defeat at second-from-bottom Motherwell on Saturday left them nine points adrift with only the slimmest mathematical chance of avoiding the drop.
Player-coaches Steve Kirk and David Kirkwood will be in charge for the rest of the season.
The job was offered to former Raith manager Jimmy Nicholl, who returned to the club after being sacked by Millwall in February, but he turned down the offer.
